days.title: Azusa to Matsumoto Castle
days.brief: Morning Azusa express from Shinjuku into the mountains. Drop bags at Nunoya Ryokan, then spend the afternoon at Matsumoto Castle and the old Nawate and Nakamachi streets. Soba and sanzoku-yaki for dinner.

items.text: Limited Express Azusa from Shinjuku (about 2 h 30 min to Matsumoto)
Walk ~15 min or taxi to Nunoya Ryokan to drop bags
Matsumoto Castle, Nawate-dori (Frog Street) and Nakamachi-dori
Shinshu soba and Sanzoku-yaki

notes: Azusa departure time is typical; check the timetable.

days.title: A simple Matsumoto day
days.brief: A slow day in Matsumoto with no trains. Make (and eat) your own soba, soak at Asama Onsen, then browse Nakamachi's storehouses and craft shops before an izakaya evening. Hand the suitcases to the ryokan for shipping to Nakatsugawa.

items.text: Morning: soba-making class, then eat what you made
Early afternoon: walk or cycle to Asama Onsen for a public-bath soak
Late afternoon: browse Nakamachi's preserved kura storehouses, craft shops and galleries
TODO: ask Nunoya Ryokan staff to ship suitcases by takkyubin (parcel delivery) to hatago STAY Shinmachi, Nakatsugawa (arriving Oct 27)
Evening: sake tasting or dinner at a local izakaya; try sanzoku-yaki (Matsumoto's marinated fried chicken)

notes: Nunoya Ryokan confirmed by email that they can arrange parcel delivery at the hotel; speak to a member of staff.
Still to confirm: hatago STAY Shinmachi can receive the suitcases before Oct 27 check-in.
Asama Onsen: historic hot-spring district close to central Matsumoto; restful without leaving town.
Craft or indigo-dye workshop: Nakamachi is the best area for small studios, textiles, paper goods and handmade souvenirs.
Japan Ukiyo-e Museum: about 3.4 km from central Matsumoto; rotating woodblock-print exhibitions with English descriptions; closed Mondays and Tuesdays (the 24th is a Saturday).
Alps Park: hillside park with views over the city and the Northern Alps; summer bobsleigh-style coaster.
Nawate Street and Yohashira Shrine: short riverside stroll with frog-themed shops, snacks and cafés.
Alternative: day trip to Kamikochi. Kamikochi Line to Shin-Shimashima, then bus (about 1 h 40 min total); hike the Azusa River: Taisho Pond, Kappa Bridge, Myojin Pond.

days.title: Torii-toge Pass: Narai to Yabuhara
days.brief: First day on the Nakasendo. Early train to Narai for coffee, then a 6 km hike over Torii-toge Pass to Yabuhara. Train on to Kiso-Fukushima and the hotel shuttle to Komanoyu for the night.

items.text: JR Chuo Main Line local 1824M from Matsumoto (bound for Nakatsugawa), arrive Narai 08:44
Coffee and something to eat in Narai
Hike Narai over Torii-toge Pass to Yabuhara station (about 6 km, 3-3.5 h)
JR Chuo Main Line local from Yabuhara to Kiso-Fukushima (or the 14:27)
Hotel shuttle meets you at Kiso-Fukushima station to Komanoyu

notes: Check-in closes at 18:00, so the 17:30 shuttle is the last safe one; call the ryokan if you are running late.
If we're hiking, ask the ryokan to pick us up at Kiso-Fukushima station at 16:30 instead of 17:30.
Trains are not hourly: other Matsumoto departures 06:32 and 10:20.
Recheck the Oct 25 JR timetable closer to travel (JR Central publishes next month's schedule monthly).

days.title: Tsumago to Magome over the pass
days.brief: The classic Nakasendo stretch. Train to Nagiso, walk the flat 4 km to Tsumago for lunch, then about 3 hours over the pass to Magome. Check in at Magome Chaya by 17:30.

items.text: Walk or shuttle to Kiso-Fukushima station (1 h, 5 km)
JR local, direct, Kiso-Fukushima to Nagiso, arrive 10:02 (backup: 11:47)
Walk Nagiso station to Tsumago via Yogawa hamlet (~4 km, mostly flat, ~40 min)
If on the later train: bus Nagiso to Tsumago (7 min) at 12:10, 12:40, 13:30 or 13:50
Tsumago: quick lunch, walk around, toilets, water and snacks
Nakasendo trail Tsumago to Magome (~8 km, ~3 h); bear bells, Tateba Tea House
Expected arrival in Magome
Check in at Magome Chaya by 17:30; traditional dinner

notes: Train times are from NAVITIME; recheck closer to the date.

days.title: Ochiai cobblestones to Nakatsugawa
days.brief: An easy-paced 9 km walk downhill from Magome to Nakatsugawa, about 4 hours with stops. Highlights are the Ochiai cobblestones and Shimogeta Bridge, ending with kurikinton in the old merchant streets. Suitcases should be waiting at hatago STAY Shinmachi.

items.text: TODO: save the Nakatsugawa city Nakasendo trail map (Nakatsugawa to Tsumago brochure) offline before setting off
Before setting off: wander Magome-juku's sloping street and the Toson Memorial Museum (former honjin, writer Shimazaki Toson); buy water and a snack
Hike Magome-juku to Nakatsugawa (~9 km, a casual 4 h; follow Nakasendo signs): Magome Castle ruins, then up and down the Jikkoku Pass; steep, take the descent slowly
Ochiai Cobblestone Path (~840 m through bamboo and woodland; ~70 m is original paving, slippery when damp)
Cross Shimogeta Bridge (Hiroshige print) into Ochiai-juku; see the honjin's gate, building and garden from outside (open Sundays only)
Continue to Nakatsugawa-juku past markers and shrines; the trail crosses Route 19 several times, follow the Nakasendo signs
Nakatsugawa-juku Honmachi merchant streets (10 min walk from JR Nakatsugawa station): sake shops, confectioners; Nakasendo Historical Museum if open
Kurikinton chestnut sweets: Nakatsugawa is its birthplace and late October is in season; shop hours vary
Check in at hatago STAY Shinmachi
Hida beef dinner

notes: Rough timings: about 4 h of casual walking with stops, Magome 09:30 to Nakatsugawa-juku around 13:30; shift everything if you start later. Route: Magome Chaya, Magome-juku, Magome Castle site, Ochiai Cobblestone Path, Ochiai-juku, Nakatsugawa-juku, hatago STAY Shinmachi.
Start early to leave daylight for sightseeing and delays.
Shoes with good grip and a light rain layer; in the wet, slow down on the cobbles rather than keep pace.
Carry water and a snack; don't count on open shops on rural stretches.
Check the day's weather and trail conditions before setting out.

days.title: Trains to Nara, Kofuku-ji and Naramachi
days.brief: Travel day out of the mountains: local train to Nagoya, Shinkansen to Kyoto, then on to Nara by about 14:30. Afternoon at Kofuku-ji and the Naramachi lanes, dinner nearby, and the hotel onsen to finish.
days.dinner: Early dinner or sake in Naramachi (Higashimuki arcade if wet)

items.text: Leave hatago STAY Shinmachi; 7 min walk to Nakatsugawa station
JR Chuo Main Line Section Rapid, Nakatsugawa to Nagoya, direct, arrive 11:37 (¥1,340)
Option A (AONIYOSHI, arrive earlier): Nozomi 25 Nagoya 12:10 to Kyoto 12:44 (¥6,660); AONIYOSHI Kyoto 12:55 to Kintetsu-Nara 13:28; walk 1.1 km to the hotel, about 13:43
Option B (Miyakoji, simpler): Nozomi 27 Nagoya 12:49 to Kyoto 13:23; Miyakoji Rapid 619 Kyoto 13:34 (platform 10) to JR Nara 14:21, direct, next to the hotel
At the hotel: leave bags or check in
Kofuku-ji: five-storey pagoda and temple grounds, about an hour
Wander the Naramachi lanes: machiya, cafés, craft shops, traditional sweets
Early dinner, local sake or a casual izakaya in Naramachi; Higashimuki Shopping Street (covered) if the weather is poor
Back to the hotel for the onsen

notes: Night 1 of 4 in Nara.
Book ahead when we arrive in Tokyo: AONIYOSHI needs a reserved seat and a limited-express ticket.
Option A: 11 min transfer at Kyoto from JR to Kintetsu; have Kintetsu tickets ready and go straight there. 33 min at Nagoya.
Option B: about 1 h 12 min wait at Nagoya; arrives JR Nara next to the hotel, close to the original 14:30 plan.
Ask the hotel about leaving bags before check-in.
Deer park moved to 29 Oct so we can walk it properly rather than rush it.

days.title: Nara Park, Todai-ji, Kasuga Taisha
days.brief: A full day on foot in Nara Park. Deer in the morning, Todai-ji's Great Buddha, lunch, then Kasuga Taisha's lantern forest. A quiet garden to wind down; the National Museum if it rains.

items.text: Enter Nara Park near Kofuku-ji; buy official shika senbei and meet the deer on the open lawns
Walk through the park to Todai-ji: Nandaimon Gate and the Great Buddha Hall
Todai-ji main hall and grounds (Nigatsu-do if time)
Lunch near the park or in Naramachi
Kasuga Taisha through the deer-filled lantern forest
Quiet finish: Yoshikien Garden (9:00–17:00, often free for foreign visitors), Ukimido Pavilion on Sagi-ike Pond, or Tobihino field
Rainy-day swap: Nara National Museum, beside the park
Local izakaya or kaki-no-ha sushi

notes: Night 2 of 4 in Nara.
Start early to beat the crowds at the park entrance; the park is open all day but the sights have set hours.
Only feed official shika senbei. Show open hands when you run out.
Keep food, maps and paper bags out of sight; the deer get pushy.
The deer are wild: don't crowd or chase them. Head to Tobihino or paths beyond the main entrance for calmer encounters.

days.title: Day trip to Kyoto: Fushimi Inari, Higashiyama, Gion
days.brief: Miyakoji Rapid to Kyoto, then straight to Fushimi Inari's torii gates. Afternoon at Kiyomizu-dera and the old Higashiyama lanes, Gion at dusk, and dinner in Pontocho before the train back to Nara.
days.dinner: Small izakaya, obanzai or noodle counter in Pontocho / Kiyamachi

items.text: JR Miyakoji Rapid, Nara to Kyoto, no transfer, arrive 11:25 (¥720); 7 min faster and 10 fewer stops than the 10:24 local
JR Nara Line, Kyoto to Inari, 2 stops, about 5 min (¥150)
Fushimi Inari Taisha: walk straight from Inari station; climb at least 15–20 min past the busy lower gates, then turn back when you like
JR back to Kyoto station, then bus 100 or 206 to Kiyomizu-michi (20–25 min total)
Kiyomizu-dera, then wander downhill through Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka; duck into a side alley or two
Kodai-ji area, Yasaka Shrine and the quiet backstreets: the best 'old Kyoto' stretch, on foot
Gion at dusk: Hanamikoji, Shirakawa canal, Tatsumi Bridge
Dinner in Pontocho or along Kiyamachi: a small izakaya, obanzai, soba/udon or ramen counter, not the first place on the busiest lane
Back to Kyoto station: bus 100/206, taxi, or Keihan Gion-Shijo to Tofukuji then JR
JR Miyakoji Rapid or local, Kyoto back to Nara (about 50 min); check the last trains

notes: Night 3 of 4 in Nara.
Use an IC card (ICOCA, Suica) for trains and buses. The ¥1,100 Subway & Bus 1-Day Pass is probably not worth it for only a couple of paid rides.
Skip Arashiyama this trip: the bamboo grove is far west and would turn the day into transport logistics.
Avoid upsells: no 'geisha experience', tea-ceremony add-ons or random rickshaw tours unless researched; the streets are the experience.
Gion after 17:00: lantern-lit lanes and a chance of seeing geiko or maiko. Photograph respectfully; never block or chase anyone.
City buses 100/206 are frequent but slow in traffic; a taxi after dinner is worth it if tired.
Golden Pavilion alternative: swap Kinkaku-ji in for Fushimi Inari. Open 09:00–17:00, ¥500, about 40 min by bus from Kyoto station; doable but more rushed.
Dropped from the earlier plan: Nintendo Museum (unconfirmed).

days.title: Day trip to Osaka: Kuromon, the Castle, Shinsekai, Dotonbori
days.brief: Food and city energy. Kintetsu to Namba, graze Kuromon Market for breakfast, Osaka Castle grounds, retro Shinsekai in the afternoon, the Umeda skyline at sunset, then neon Dotonbori and Hozenji Yokocho for dinner.
days.dinner: Hozenji Yokocho or a small Namba izakaya

items.text: Kintetsu Nara Line, Kintetsu-Nara to Osaka-Namba, about 40 min (¥680, IC card)
Arrive Osaka-Namba; buy the ¥620 Enjoy Eco Card (Metro + city bus day pass, Saturday price)
Kuromon Ichiba Market as breakfast: grilled seafood, tamagoyaki, wagyu skewers, fruit, coffee. One or two small things per stall; follow the locals' queues
Metro Nippombashi to Tanimachi 4-chome (Chuo Line)
Osaka Castle: park, moat, stone walls and exterior views (free); enter the keep only for the museum and viewing floor
Metro Tanimachi 4-chome to Dobutsuen-mae via Namba
Shinsekai and Tsutenkaku: retro Showa streets, kushikatsu lunch, Janjan Yokocho; wander a street or two beyond
Metro to Umeda; browse or rest with coffee
Umeda Sky Building for sunset; arrive early for the viewing-deck queue
Metro back to Namba: Dotonbori canal, then Hozenji Yokocho, dinner
Kintetsu, Osaka-Namba back to Kintetsu-Nara, about 40 min (¥680)

notes: Night 4 of 4 in Nara.
The Enjoy Eco Card (¥620 on weekends) covers all Osaka Metro lines and city buses, not the Kintetsu legs from Nara.
Saturday is busy at Kuromon, Dotonbori and the Sky Building; the early Kuromon start and pre-sunset Umeda arrival are the crowd-avoidance moves.
Kuromon: some stalls charge premium prices for photogenic skewers. Simple grilled fish, oden or sushi is better value.
Shinsekai: ignore the pushiest touts; pick a busy, established kushikatsu counter.
Glico running man: quick photo, then the side streets around Dotonbori and Hozenji.
Skip Universal Studios: it would take the whole day.
Calmer option: drop the Sky Building and spend 17:00 onward in Nakazakicho (vintage shops, cafés, small bars near Umeda).
Lots of walking: comfortable shoes.
